lesson.menu_desc: Check in at a hotel in Berlin and ask for what you need -- can / can't
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 5 -- The Front Desk
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Camillo Furlan Alfredini | Lesson 5 -- The Front Desk
lesson.grammar_point: can / can't (requests, permission and ability: Can I...? Can you...? I can't...)

listenings.text: Welcome to the Hotel Spree in Berlin. Check-in is from three p.m., and check-out is at eleven a.m. Breakfast is from six thirty to ten, on the first floor. You can use the gym from six a.m. to ten p.m. You can't smoke in the rooms. If you need help, you can call the front desk at any time. Enjoy your stay!

Hi, I'm Lucas, from Brazil. I travel a lot for work. In a hotel, I always ask three things. Can I check in early? Can I have a quiet room? I can't sleep with noise. And what is the Wi-Fi password? In Germany, the people at the front desk can speak English very well, so it is easy. My English is not perfect, but I can say what I need.

extra_audio.text: Camillo arrives at a hotel in Berlin at noon. He goes to the front desk. He asks: Can I check in now? The receptionist says: I'm sorry, you can't. Check-in is at three. He leaves his bag at the hotel and goes for a walk. At three o'clock, he gets his room key and goes up in the elevator.
